before.target: Senior review of supplier payments: in place across everything it should cover.
activities: Agree the design with the finance lead, so that it meets the target standard.
Review the first full cycle against M27.
before.measure: Records for the period show this practice applied to every case in scope: senior review of supplier payments.

after.target: Each month a senior manager who does not process payments reviews the list of supplier payments for unfamiliar suppliers, unusual amounts and changed bank details, and follows up each query.
activities: Define the patterns to look for in supplier payments and the report, query or alert that finds them.
Name who reviews the output monthly and who follows up each exception, independently of the people whose activity is reviewed.
Run the review over the last twelve months of data, and follow up what it finds.
after.records: Monthly payment review: the list reviewed, the reviewer, each query raised and its answer.
after.measure: The review of supplier payments ran monthly throughout the period, and every exception it raised has a recorded answer.
after.onFailure: Where an exception proves to be fraud or error, follow the response procedure, correct the control that allowed it and add the pattern to the review.

before.target: Every new supplier goes through a defined process, with set checks and an approval, before it can be paid.
activities: Agree the design with the procurement lead, so that it meets the target standard at level 4.
Keep the records in E01.
Review the first full cycle against M01.
before.records: The onboarding procedure, completed onboarding files for a sample of new suppliers, exception reports.
before.measure: Records for the period show that every new supplier goes through a defined process, with set checks and an approval, before it can be paid.

after.target: Every new supplier passes set checks, including registration, tax number, bank account and directors, and is approved before it can be paid.
activities: Set out the check in the procedure for new suppliers: what is checked, by whom, and who may approve an exception.
Set the supplier master file so that no new supplier proceeds until the check is recorded as passed.
Look back over new suppliers from the last twelve months, and follow up any that would not have passed the check.
after.records: Supplier set-up file: the result and source of each check, who captured the supplier and who approved it.
after.measure: Every new supplier in the period has a supplier set-up file showing each check passed and an approval dated before the first payment.
after.cycle: before each new supplier is first paid
after.onFailure: Where a new supplier went ahead without the check, complete the check at once and review anything paid or released before it was found.

before.target: Takings at every cash point are reconciled to sales records daily, and every shortage and surplus is investigated.
activities: Agree the design with the operations lead, so that it meets the target standard at level 4.
Keep the records in E24.
Review the first full cycle against M43.
before.records: Daily reconciliation sheets, the shortages and surpluses log, investigation notes.
before.measure: Records for the period show that takings at every cash point are reconciled to sales records daily, and every shortage and surplus is investigated.

after.target: Takings at every cash point are reconciled to sales records daily, and every shortage and surplus is investigated.
activities: Set the reconciliation: what is compared, how often (daily), who prepares it and who reviews it.
Keep a log of differences with the explanation and outcome of each, and a threshold above which a difference is escalated.
Review the first month of reconciliations and differences, and correct the procedure where differences were left open.
after.records: Daily cash reconciliation: takings at each cash point compared with sales records, the preparer and reviewer, and each shortage or surplus with its explanation.
after.measure: Every daily cash reconciliation due in the period was completed and reviewed, and every difference has a recorded explanation.
after.onFailure: Investigate any difference left unexplained, and escalate repeated differences at the same point or involving the same person.

before.target: AI methods tested per process: in place across everything it should cover.
activities: Establish which answer is correct. The answers about AI-enabled fraud cannot both be right as given: one says AI-enabled schemes are assessed for every relevant process, the other that the assessment does not ask, process by process, how AI could be used against it.
Agree the design with the fraud risk lead, so that it meets the target standard.
Review the first full cycle against M03.
before.measure: Records for the period show this practice applied to every case in scope: AI methods tested per process.

after.target: For each high-risk process, the assessment asks how AI could be used against it, for example whether a cloned voice could pass a call-back check, and records the answer.
activities: Establish which of the conflicting answers reflects how the process runs, and correct the record.
Add a question, for each high-risk process, on how AI could be used against it to the fraud risk assessment method and to the template it uses.
Apply it at the next assessment or update, starting with processes that rely on a call-back, a signature or a document.
Have the person who signs off the assessment confirm that it meets the requirement.
after.records: Fraud risk register: for each high-risk process, the AI methods considered and whether existing controls would stop them.
after.measure: The assessment current at the end of the period shows the question asked and answered for every high-risk process.
after.onFailure: Record any part of the assessment that does not meet the requirement as an open item with an owner, and complete it before the next sign-off.
after.pattern: A requirement of the fraud risk assessment
